purpose: LRM 4.6.4.4 noise_table_log: no extrapolation below or above the table

oracle.derivation: Same 500 ohm flat transfer impedance. Table (1e3,1e-18) (1e6,1e-24). LRM 4.6.4.4: 'As with noise_table(), for frequencies lower than the lowest frequency in the value set, noise_table_log() returns the power specified for the lowest frequency, and for frequencies higher than the highest frequency, noise_table_log() returns the power specified for the highest frequency.' f=500 Hz < 1000 Hz so S_I = 1.0e-18 and onoise = 500*1e-9 = 5.0e-07 V/sqrt(Hz); the -2 slope EXTRAPOLATED would have read 4e-18 and 1.0e-06, i.e. exactly 2x, so a host that runs the formula past the first knot fails here. f=2e6 Hz > 1e6 Hz so S_I = 1.0e-24, the top row, and onoise = 500*1e-12 = 5.0e-10 V/sqrt(Hz); the extrapolated slope would have read 2.5e-25 and 2.5e-10. The high point also pins the top tabulated power itself, since the clamp returns that row verbatim.
